Explanation

Your application has hardcoded URLs that might correspond to services that are not accessible on Azure.

Review and ensure that the application is attempting to access URLs that would be available from Azure. You might need to migrate those services to Azure too, this way you will get the benefit of lower latency in the cloud.

If your application needs to depend on services that run on-premises, you can connect your Azure and local networks with ExpressRoute, Hybrid Connections, or VPN solutions.
SQL database connection detected
 Potential 3
FilePosition
src\eShopWCFService\Web.config

Explanation

SQL database connection detected.

Ensure the database is available/reachable on Azure.

If it is not, there are multiple ways you can move your data to Azure:
1. Migrate to Azure SQL Database.
2. Consider Azure SQL Managed Instance if you need features that are not available in Azure SQL Database and you don’t want to use a VM.
3. Migrate your database servers directly to SQL Server on Azure VMs.

To assess database migration effort, you can use Azure Migrate tool, see the link below.
Local or network IO operations detected
 Potential 3
FilePosition
src\eShopWinForms\Views\CatalogView.csLine 57

Explanation

Your application has local or network IO operations.

If you are targeting Managed Instance on Azure App Service, move persistent I/O to storage mounts (Azure Files/UNC). Keep local writes to temp only; connect to external dependencies via private endpoints/VNet to reduce latency.

IO operations outside of the application folder might not be available on Azure App Service. Review and ensure IO APIs are attempting to access paths that will be available when your app is running on App Service sandbox. If you choose the containerized hosting option, your scenario still might be broken or have scalability issues.

Possible solutions:
1. Files that the application needs can be deployed with the application or put in Azure Storage. You can use Azure Storage File Shares as a drop-in replacement for on-premises file share.
2. Other services that the application depends on might need to be migrated to Azure, this way you will get the benefit of lower latency in the cloud.
3. If your application needs to depend on services that run on-premise, you can connect your Azure and local networks with ExpressRoute, Hybrid Connections, or VPN solutions.
Local OS environment access detected
 Potential 1
FilePosition
src\eShopWinForms\Views\CatalogView.csLine 56

Explanation

Local OS environment access detected.

If you are targeting Managed Instance on Azure App Service, Read config via App Settings or App Configuration; avoid machine‑specific environment APIs. Persist environment setup via install scripts when needed.

When running in Azure App Service environment, your application can read environment variables that you define in App Service settings. Using environment API other than reading environment variables might indicate that your application depends on some local machine's features and might be broken on App Service sandbox or not scale well. Review your scenarios and either refactor them to be more cloud friendly or choose the option in App Service to host your application in the sandbox for Windows Container Web Apps.

If you choose to use other Azure hosting options such as Azure Container Apps (ACA) or Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS), environment APIs might work, however scaling still might be an issue.
Upgrade to newer target framework to get better cloud experience
 Optional 3
FilePosition
src\eShopWCFService\eShopWCFService.csproj
src\eShopWinForms\eShopWinForms.csproj

Explanation

Upgrade to newer target framework to get better cloud experience.

If you are targeting Managed Instance on Azure App Service, validate on .NET Framework 4.8 or move to .NET 10. Persist any runtime prerequisites via install scripts; test in staging before production.

While if targeting other Azure compute services:

Application targeting .NET framework lower than 4.7.1 might missing features that would be needed for some cloud scenarios like scaling or getting secrets from secure external sources.

Azure App Service runs apps on .NET Framework 4.8 or .NET Framework 3.5. Apps running on on .NET Framework versions older than .NET Framework 4.8 could have potential compatibility issues. It is recommended to test your application running on .NET Framework 4.8. Note that it is not necessary to re-target to .NET Framework 4.8, only to validate that the app correctly runs on that version of .NET Framework.

In the long term it is also recommended to upgrade your application to latest supported .NET 8+ which would significantly increase performance of your application. Use tools like .NET Upgrade Assistant to help with upgrading your application to newer .NET.
Connection strings without configuration builders detected
 Optional 3
FilePosition

src\eShopWCFService\Web.config

Explanation

Connection strings without configuration builders detected.

Keeping connection strings directly in the app is not the best practice and might introduce security risks, increased maintenance, scalability challenges or compliance standards (such as PCI DSS, GDPR, etc.).

Instead, it is recommended to use configuration builders to get secrets from secure sources in Azure environment.
System.Data.SqlClient dependency detected
 Optional 3
FilePosition
src\eShopWCFService\Web.config

Explanation

System.Data.SqlClient dependency is detected.

While System.Data.SqlClient will work in Azure, the newer Microsoft.Data.SqlClient package is the primary .NET SQL client moving forward and receiving the latest features. For example, Microsoft.Data.SqlClient easily allows use of Azure Managed Identity from a connection string.

Explanation

Static content detected.

Your current approach of serving static content directly might lead to increased costs, performance issues, maintenance challenges (requiring application redeployment for content changes), and security risks.

Consider moving static content to Azure Blob Storage and adding Azure CDN.

WCF Client APIs
 Mandatory 1
FilePosition

Explanation

WCF client-side APIs for building service clients that communicate with WCF services. These APIs are available as exact equivalents via NuGet packages - add System.ServiceModel.* NuGet packages (System.ServiceModel.Http, System.ServiceModel.Primitives, System.ServiceModel.NetTcp, etc.)
Legacy Configuration System
 Mandatory 2
FilePosition

Explanation

Legacy XML-based configuration system (app.config/web.config) that has been replaced by a more flexible configuration model in .NET Core. The old system was rigid and XML-based. Migrate to Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration with JSON/environment variables; use System.Configuration.ConfigurationManager NuGet package as interim bridge if needed.
GDI+ / System.Drawing
 Mandatory 1
FilePosition

Explanation

System.Drawing APIs for 2D graphics, imaging, and printing that are available via NuGet package System.Drawing.Common. Note: Not recommended for server scenarios due to Windows dependencies; consider cross-platform alternatives like SkiaSharp or ImageSharp for new code.
Windows Forms Legacy Controls
 Mandatory 3
FilePosition

Explanation

Legacy Windows Forms controls that have been removed from .NET Core/5+ including StatusBar, DataGrid, ContextMenu, MainMenu, MenuItem, and ToolBar. These controls were replaced by more modern alternatives. Use ToolStrip, MenuStrip, ContextMenuStrip, and DataGridView instead.
Windows Forms
 Mandatory 1
FilePosition

Explanation

Windows Forms APIs for building Windows desktop applications with traditional Forms-based UI that are available in .NET on Windows. Enable Windows Desktop support: Option 1 (Recommended): Target net9.0-windows; Option 2: Add <UseWindowsDesktop>true</UseWindowsDesktop>; Option 3 (Legacy): Use Microsoft.NET.Sdk.WindowsDesktop SDK.

Data Storage & External Services

The server owns a SQL Server database via EntityModel; its default connection names LocalDB and eShopDatabase. An environment connection override can select another database connection (src\eShopWCFService\Models\Infrastructure\CatalogConfiguration.cs:10-18). Five DbSets cover catalog, classifications, stock and discounts (src\eShopWCFService\EntityModel.cs:18-22). The desktop loads images from local files, not a media service (src\eShopWinForms\Views\CatalogView.cs:55-61). No broker, distributed cache, cloud service or additional remote API is evidenced in this scoped application.

Key Architectural Decisions

  • The desktop uses view/controller separation and manual constructor injection; Program composes the real generated proxy and view without a DI container (src\eShopWinForms\Program.cs:22-27; src\eShopWinForms\Controllers\CatalogController.cs:14-20).
  • Service operations contain business rules and access DbContext directly; there is no separate repository abstraction (src\eShopWCFService\CatalogService.svc.cs:14-30,56-82,90-117).
  • Domain entities double as mutable WCF data contracts; database creation and seed data are code-first initializer responsibilities (src\eShopWCFService\Models\CatalogItem.cs:10-35; src\eShopWCFService\EntityModel.cs:12-16).

API & Service Communication Contracts

The scoped application exposes ten SOAP operations at one WCF service address, consumed synchronously by the desktop. These are operation-based SOAP contracts, not ten REST routes.

DTOs & Contracts

Entities are annotated with DataContract/DataMember and use WCF data-contract serialization, not a JSON REST serializer (src\eShopWCFService\Models\CatalogItem.cs:10-35; src\eShopWCFService\Models\CatalogBrand.cs:10-19; src\eShopWCFService\Models\CatalogType.cs:10-19; src\eShopWCFService\Models\CatalogItemsStock.cs:10-25; src\eShopWCFService\Models\DiscountItem.cs:11-31). See data-architecture.md for entity fields and mappings.

No gateway-level composite DTOs exist. WSDL/XSD artifacts and the generated mutable client models are checked into src\eShopWinForms\Connected Services\eShopServiceReference; the build explicitly includes Reference.cs (src\eShopWinForms\eShopWinForms.csproj:89-93,258-264). No OpenAPI, protobuf or GraphQL contract is present.

Contract drift: the generated client accepts nullable filter IDs and returns arrays, while the current server interface accepts non-nullable ints and returns Lists (src\eShopWinForms\Connected Services\eShopServiceReference\Reference.cs:507-523; src\eShopWCFService\ICatalogService.cs:18-22). The running controller supplies concrete int values; null compatibility is not verified.

Communication Patterns

  • Synchronous: UI events call the controller, then generated proxy operations; server calls EntityModel directly (src\eShopWinForms\Controllers\CatalogController.cs:35-54,75-84; src\eShopWCFService\CatalogService.svc.cs:18-30).
  • Async: generated Task alternatives exist but the active controller uses synchronous methods. These are client async wrappers, not broker/event-driven communication (src\eShopWinForms\Connected Services\eShopServiceReference\Reference.cs:501-559).
  • Composition: the controller fetches items and the current discount separately and combines them for display; no gateway, multi-backend join, discovery registry or load balancing is configured (src\eShopWinForms\Controllers\CatalogController.cs:75-84).
  • Resilience: no retry, circuit breaker, bulkhead or service fallback is implemented. No timeout values are explicitly configured: the empty named basicHttpBinding uses framework defaults, not application-declared values (src\eShopWinForms\App.config:20-28). Exceptions from service calls are not caught by the controller.
  • Startup: database access must be usable when the service handles initial calls; Program loads all view data before showing its dialog. No readiness gate or startup retry exists in that flow (src\eShopWinForms\Program.cs:22-27). See configuration-inventory.md.
  • Security: the checked-in client and explicit service endpoint use HTTP basicHttpBinding with no configured transport credentials, authentication or operation authorization. HTTPS protocol mapping and HTTPS metadata are declared but do not make the explicit HTTP endpoint/client TLS-protected. IIS/deployment controls cannot be inferred (src\eShopWCFService\Web.config:22-42; src\eShopWinForms\App.config:19-29). No typed fault policy is declared; exception details in faults are disabled.

Core Business Workflows

The application lets operators browse a product catalog, see date-based promotions, look up stock for a selected day and record a product's stock availability. No basket, checkout, payment or order-fulfillment workflow is implemented in the scoped application.

Domain Entities

EntityService / Bounded ContextDescriptionKey Relationships
CatalogItemCatalogService / catalog managementProduct description, selling price and image referenceClassified by brand and type; referenced by dated stock
CatalogBrandCatalogService / catalog classificationProduct brand classificationShared classification for products
CatalogTypeCatalogService / catalog classificationProduct type classificationShared classification for products
CatalogItemsStockCatalogService / availabilityQuantity available for a product on a calendar dayLogical product association; not an accumulated movement ledger
DiscountItemCatalogService / promotionsPromotion fraction valid during a date intervalApplied globally to displayed products; no per-product association

Evidence: src\eShopWCFService\Models\CatalogItem.cs:11-35; src\eShopWCFService\Models\CatalogBrand.cs:11-19; src\eShopWCFService\Models\CatalogType.cs:11-19; src\eShopWCFService\Models\CatalogItemsStock.cs:12-25; src\eShopWCFService\Models\DiscountItem.cs:12-31; src\eShopWinForms\Views\CatalogView.cs:48-61.

Service-to-Domain Mapping

ServiceDomain ContextOwned EntitiesExternal Dependencies
CatalogServiceCatalog, classification, promotion and dated availability; one combined service boundaryAll five domain entitiesPersistence through EntityModel
Desktop CatalogController / CatalogViewOperator interaction and presentation compositionNo authoritative persisted entities; consumes copiesRemote CatalogService and local images

This is a single business service with a desktop client, not separately deployed bounded-context microservices. EntityModel's five sets and the desktop service injection establish the ownership boundary (src\eShopWCFService\EntityModel.cs:18-22; src\eShopWinForms\Program.cs:22-27).

Primary Workflows

Workflow 1: Browse and filter catalog with current promotion

  1. Program constructs the remote client, view and controller. LoadView sets the controller, checks promotions, loads initial products, loads classification filters, then loads shipment-product choices (src\eShopWinForms\Program.cs:22-27; src\eShopWinForms\Controllers\CatalogController.cs:150-157).
  2. A brand/type selection raises a filter event. The controller clears the grid and retrieves matching products under the zero-means-all filtering rule (src\eShopWinForms\Views\CatalogView.cs:106-135; src\eShopWinForms\Controllers\CatalogController.cs:27-29,75-78).
  3. The service applies selected classifications after materializing products. The controller separately asks for today's promotion under the inclusive promotion window rule (src\eShopWCFService\CatalogService.svc.cs:28-30,56-62; src\eShopWinForms\Controllers\CatalogController.cs:79-84).
  4. The view computes display prices under the global display discount rule, loads local product thumbnails and appends grid rows (src\eShopWinForms\Views\CatalogView.cs:48-61).
  5. On initial load, an active promotion also sets banner text. The banner check is separate from the discount lookup used for prices (src\eShopWinForms\Controllers\CatalogController.cs:60-69).

No service-availability fallback exists. An image or service exception is not handled in this path; the grid may already have been cleared. The initial data load runs before the main dialog is shown.

Workflow 2: Record dated stock availability

  1. The operator selects a product and enters quantity/date. The view applies shipment input presence checks, then parses values and emits the shipment event (src\eShopWinForms\Views\CatalogView.cs:157-167).
  2. The controller creates a stock contract and sends it to the service (src\eShopWinForms\Controllers\CatalogController.cs:35-42).
  3. The service finds the first matching product/calendar-day record. Under the replace-not-add stock rule, it overwrites that record's quantity; otherwise it creates a record using manual stock ID allocation (src\eShopWCFService\CatalogService.svc.cs:99-117).
  4. A successful response causes a confirmation dialog and clears shipment inputs. There is no automatic stock re-query or replenishment accumulation (src\eShopWinForms\Controllers\CatalogController.cs:42-43; src\eShopWinForms\Views\CatalogView.cs:189-195).

Workflow 3: Query stock for a product and day

  1. The user selects a product and calendar date; the view extracts the product ID from displayed text and raises a search event (src\eShopWinForms\Views\CatalogView.cs:142-151).
  2. The controller requests stock; the service applies the first matching stock or zero rule (src\eShopWinForms\Controllers\CatalogController.cs:50-54; src\eShopWCFService\CatalogService.svc.cs:90-96).
  3. The view appends a result row with date, product and availability rather than replacing earlier results (src\eShopWinForms\Views\CatalogView.cs:173-182).

Workflow 4: Initialize demonstration data and maintain catalog records

The first database creation seeds classifications, products, stock and promotions using predefined samples; this is not a scheduled recurring process (src\eShopWCFService\Models\Infrastructure\CatalogDBInitializer.cs:11-20). Promotion/stock sample dates are in 2017 (src\eShopWCFService\Models\Infrastructure\PreconfiguredData.cs:41-75).

The service also exposes product creation, update and deletion. Creation uses manual product ID allocation; updates mark the supplied entity modified; deletion removes the supplied entity, each followed by SaveChanges. The active desktop controller does not initiate these catalog mutations (src\eShopWCFService\CatalogService.svc.cs:65-82; src\eShopWinForms\Controllers\CatalogController.cs:35-157).

Cross-Service Data Flows

Only the desktop-to-CatalogService boundary is present. CatalogService is the source of truth for products, classifications, stock and promotions; the desktop composes product and promotion responses locally into discounted rows. Separate classification calls populate filter controls; stock requests reference the chosen product ID (src\eShopWinForms\Controllers\CatalogController.cs:35-54,75-84,98-143).

There is no gateway aggregation across multiple backend services, event choreography, broker or compensating workflow. If a call fails, the controller has no retry/circuit-breaker fallback or substitute service, so no intentionally degraded business response is defined. The service mock is not wired into the live desktop flow and its promotion method is unimplemented (src\eShopWinForms\Program.cs:23; src\eShopWCFService\CatalogServiceMock.cs:118-120).

Business Rules & Decision Logic

RuleImplemented decisionEvidence

Validation gapsNo explicit positive quantity/price rule, promotion fraction range, start-before-end check or per-product/date uniqueness check is implementedEntity annotations and src\eShopWCFService\CatalogService.svc.cs:28-30,65-82,99-117

State transitions and integrity: stock is inserted or replaced; there is no shipment lifecycle/status machine, order lifecycle or running stock ledger. Product navigations are populated explicitly during individual item lookup, without inverse collection maintenance (src\eShopWCFService\CatalogService.svc.cs:33-44).

Transactions: each service mutation uses an individual SaveChanges. Lookup and max-ID selection are not wrapped with the write in a declared encompassing transaction; no saga or compensation exists. Initializer groups are separately saved (src\eShopWCFService\CatalogService.svc.cs:65-82,99-117; src\eShopWCFService\Models\Infrastructure\CatalogDBInitializer.cs:22-79).

Errors: there are no business exception types, controller catch handlers, dead-letter paths or idempotency keys in these flows. Quantity/date parse failures, missing stock-search selection and missing images can throw; a response lost after a successful save has no explicit reconciliation path (src\eShopWinForms\Views\CatalogView.cs:55-59,142-164).

Authorization and audit: no role/ownership checks or business audit trail are implemented in the examined controller/service code. A desktop success MessageBox is a user notification, not durable audit logging (src\eShopWinForms\Views\CatalogView.cs:189-195; src\eShopWCFService\CatalogService.svc.cs:14-118). Infrastructure-level controls outside the scoped source remain unknown.

Version & Compatibility Risks

The server targets the retired .NET Framework 4.6.1 release, while the desktop targets 4.7; deployment support also depends on the installed framework/Windows lifecycle. EF6 6.1.3, Web API Client 5.2.3 and Newtonsoft.Json 6.0.4 are old declarations and need compatibility and advisory review before modernization. This dependency inventory is not a vulnerability scan and does not claim CVE verification. Classic System.Web hosting, desktop Windows Forms and WCF server hosting are material portability considerations (src\eShopWCFService\eShopWCFService.csproj:10-18,64-68; src\eShopWinForms\eShopWinForms.csproj:8-11,85).

Notable Observations

  • Both projects carry EF6; the package ledger alone does not establish that the desktop accesses a database (src\eShopWinForms\packages.config:3).
  • Packages use packages.config and sibling ..\packages\... hint paths, not SDK PackageReference or central package management (src\eShopWCFService\eShopWCFService.csproj:45-49; src\eShopWinForms\eShopWinForms.csproj:57-74).
  • No project-to-project reference is declared. The solution contains two projects, while the desktop explicitly compiles a generated service reference (eShopLegacyNTier.sln:6-9; src\eShopWinForms\eShopWinForms.csproj:89-93).
  • No lock file or resolved transitive dependency graph is present in scope; declared package relationships must not be mistaken for a verified transitive tree. A .NET 3.5 SP1 bootstrapper entry is disabled and is not an active package/runtime target (src\eShopWinForms\eShopWinForms.csproj:270-274).

Key Repository Methods

There is no repository interface: CatalogService queries EntityModel's DbSets directly. Standard EF DbSet CRUD is therefore not presented as an inherited application repository contract.

No raw SQL, stored procedure, cross-service batch finder or paging query is present in the implementation. Catalog creation similarly allocates max ID plus one (src\eShopWCFService\CatalogService.svc.cs:65-70).

Caching Strategy

No cache provider, cache region, TTL, eviction policy, session cache, query-result cache or second-level cache is declared in the scoped configurations and package manifests. EF context tracking is not an application caching strategy. The desktop re-fetches products and discounts when filters change (src\eShopWinForms\Controllers\CatalogController.cs:75-84).

CatalogServiceMock owns in-memory sample lists, but it is an alternate implementation and not a cache in front of persistence; the active Program uses the generated remote client (src\eShopWCFService\CatalogServiceMock.cs:18-23; src\eShopWinForms\Program.cs:22-24).

Data Ownership Boundaries

A single service owns one store; this is neither database-per-microservice nor a shared database accessed by multiple active service modules. The desktop crosses a SOAP boundary and receives serialized copies. No direct desktop DbContext use is evidenced in its compiled controller/composition path despite its EF package declaration (src\eShopWinForms\Controllers\CatalogController.cs:10-20,75-84; src\eShopWinForms\Program.cs:22-27).

Reads and writes share the same service and model; there is no CQRS split, outbox, broker-based propagation or eventual-consistency implementation. The desktop combines product data with a separate discount response for presentation, without joining a second service's database (src\eShopWinForms\Controllers\CatalogController.cs:75-84).
